akk.name: Akkadian (transliteration)
akk.note: The Akkadian of each line from the best-preserved copy, in transliteration, as edited by SEAL (Sources of Early Akkadian Literature, M. P. Streck and N. Wasserman, Leipzig and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, seal.huji.ac.il), with SEAL's line labels: Tablet I by line, Tablet II by SEAL's segments (A-I, in story order), Tablet III by column. Square brackets mark words restored where the clay is broken, usually from another copy or a repeated passage; "x" is a sign that cannot be read. Most lines come from the copy written by the junior scribe Ipiq-Aya at Sippar in the reign of Ammi-saduqa, king of Babylon (its colophons give 1,245 lines for the three tablets); later copies, down to Neo-Assyrian and Late Babylonian times, fill its gaps.
